newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs firm in busy week.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs firm in busy week.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates firmed in a busy week with owners optimistic that the market will rise further, brokers said on Friday.

E.A. Gibson said in their weekly tanker report that some 30 large vessels obtained employment from the Mideast Gulf, totalling about 8.75 million tonnes, and remarkably, 12 of these were ultra-large crude carriers (ULCCs).

Voyages to the east predominated, but not to the same extent as recently. Estimated availability between now and August 8 stands at some 42 vessels of 12 million tonnes, of which 31 are VLCCs and 11 ULCCs, Gibson said.
VLCCs going east were fixed at a healthy W70/72.5 and to the west at W62.5, while ULCCs to the Red Sea fetched W55.

Brokers Galbraith's Ltd said ULCCs could in fact have fetched higher rates "but a combination of secrecy and the fact that previous weeks had been quiet enabled charterers to 'keep a lid on the situation'."

But Suezmaxes (130,000 tonne vessels) all dipped, and have fallen from a year-high of W105 in March to W85 for West Africa/USAC voyages and W80 for West Africa/U.K./Cont, according to a Galbraith's chart.

Galbraith's said that often when West Africa is quiet, other sectors take up the slack, but this had not been the case over the last week, noting that the Donat was fixed Libya/Trieste at a modest W85.

But they added, "Despite the foregoing the market is actually more finely balanced than many perceive and it would not actually take a vast increase in activity to push the market back into the W90s."
Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) were also mainly slack with 72,000 tonnes Mexico/upcoast as low as W125 against W145 last week and over W200 a few weeks ago.
North Sea Aframaxes dipped to W100, and although enquiry in the Mediterranean increased, this failed to push rates up from about W120/122.5, brokers said.
The only Aframax sector to firm was the busy Indonesia/Japan-South Korea run which edged up to W120.
